items.title: Account Associate - Austin
items.description: ABOUT THE TEAM OpenAI’s Enterprise Go-To-Market organization helps the world’s largest companies adopt and scale our AI platform across their business from ChatGPT Enterprise to our developer platform and APIs. We partner with organizations across the enterprise to build new AI-powered customer experiences, transform operations, and reimagine how work gets done in highly regulated and technically complex environments. As adoption accelerates through pilots, experimentation, and developer-led use cases, the GTM team turns that momentum into durable, enterprise-wide deployments. Account Associates sit at the front of this motion where technical curiosity turns into executive engagement, and early product signals become enterprise-wide deployments. ABOUT THE ROLE As an Account Associate, you’ll help our Enterprise teams turn product usage, pilots, inbound interest, and targeted outreach into qualified enterprise opportunities. Working alongside Account Directors, you’ll apply your sales experience to discovery, stakeholder mapping, and account strategy while deepening your ability to navigate complex enterprise opportunities. You’ll exercise judgment in handling discovery and qualification assignments, evaluating differing stakeholder needs and recommending next steps while drawing on Account Directors for guidance on more complex issues. We are looking for individuals with 2–4 years of professional sales experience in SDR/BDR roles, full-cycle Account Executive roles, or a combination of both. Candidates should be motivated to build on that experience and grow into world-class enterprise sellers. This role can lead to opportunities as an Account Director or in other GTM roles, with progression based on performance and business needs rather than a fixed timeline. For the right person, this is an opportunity to build on an established sales foundation and develop a long-term career in AI go-to-market. This role is based in Austin, TX. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week (Monday through Wednesday) and offer relocation assistance to new employees. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL - Partner with Account Directors on account strategy, multi-threading, and deal progression. Assess account developments and recommend adjustments to engagement approaches within agreed priorities. - Design and execute targeted outbound strategies using industry context, stakeholder mapping, and product signal to break into priority accounts. - Lead high-quality discovery to uncover business priorities, map stakeholders, and assess enterprise readiness. Evaluate differing stakeholder needs and incomplete information to recommend qualification decisions and next steps. - Contribute to pipeline reviews by sharing outbound activity, account insights, and early competitive signals. - Build and iterate on AI-enabled GTM workflows (GPTs/agents) to scale prospecting and qualification. YOU MAY THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU - Have 2–4 years of professional sales experience in SDR/BDR roles, full-cycle Account Executive roles, or a combination of both, with demonstrated success in your assigned responsibilities. Experience working at a startup or selling enterprise SaaS is strongly preferred. - Have a track record of meeting or exceeding quota or measurable sales targets, such as qualified pipeline, sales opportunities, or revenue, with clear examples of your individual contribution. - Demonstrate strong business acumen and can lead discovery conversations that uncover customer priorities, connect potential solutions to measurable outcomes, and establish clear next steps. - Have experience researching accounts, developing targeted outreach, and engaging business and technical stakeholders to generate qualified opportunities. Experience prospecting into enterprise or strategic accounts is a plus. - Have a strong interest in AI, regularly experiment with AI tools, and can connect their capabilities to practical business needs. - Use performance data and feedback to refine your approach, and show persistence when outreach or opportunities do not progress as expected. - Are comfortable with ambiguity, moving quickly, and taking ownership of your work while collaborating closely with Account Directors. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement https://cdn.openai.com/policies/eeo-policy-statement.pdf. Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations. No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made via this link https://form.asana.com/?k=bQ7w9h3iexRlicUdWRiwvg&d=57018692298241. As adoption accelerates through pilots, experimentation, and developer-led use cases, the GTM team turns that momentum into durable, enterprise-wide deployments. Account Associates sit at the front of this motion—where technical curiosity turns into executive engagement, and early product signals become enterprise-wide deployments. ABOUT THE ROLE As an Account Associate, you’ll help our Enterprise teams turn product usage, pilots, inbound interest, and targeted outreach into qualified enterprise opportunities. Working alongside Account Directors, you’ll apply your sales experience to discovery, stakeholder mapping, and account strategy while deepening your ability to navigate complex enterprise opportunities. You’ll exercise judgment in handling discovery and qualification assignments, evaluating differing stakeholder needs and recommending next steps while drawing on Account Directors for guidance on more complex issues. We are looking for individuals with 2–4 years of professional sales experience in SDR/BDR roles, full-cycle Account Executive roles, or a combination of both. Candidates should be motivated to build on that experience and grow into world-class enterprise sellers. This role can lead to opportunities as an Account Director or in other GTM roles, with progression based on performance and business needs rather than a fixed timeline. For the right person, this is an opportunity to build on an established sales foundation and develop a long-term career in AI go-to-market. This role is based in New York, New York. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week (Monday through Wednesday) and offer relocation assistance to new employees. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL - Partner with Account Directors on account strategy, multi-threading, and deal progression. Assess account developments and recommend adjustments to engagement approaches within agreed priorities. - Design and execute targeted outbound strategies using industry context, stakeholder mapping, and product signal to break into priority accounts. - Lead high-quality discovery to uncover business priorities, map stakeholders, and assess enterprise readiness. Evaluate differing stakeholder needs and incomplete information to recommend qualification decisions and next steps. - Contribute to pipeline reviews by sharing outbound activity, account insights, and early competitive signals. - Build and iterate on AI-enabled GTM workflows (GPTs/agents) to scale prospecting and qualification. YOU MAY THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU - Have 2–4 years of professional sales experience in SDR/BDR roles, full-cycle Account Executive roles, or a combination of both, with demonstrated success in your assigned responsibilities. Experience working at a startup or selling enterprise SaaS is strongly preferred. - Have a track record of meeting or exceeding quota or measurable sales targets, such as qualified pipeline, sales opportunities, or revenue, with clear examples of your individual contribution. - Demonstrate strong business acumen and can lead discovery conversations that uncover customer priorities, connect potential solutions to measurable outcomes, and establish clear next steps. - Have experience researching accounts, developing targeted outreach, and engaging business and technical stakeholders to generate qualified opportunities. items.title: CMC & Manufacturing Lead, Life Sciences
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic’s Life Sciences team is working to make Claude a useful partner across biology and drug development, so that promising science can reach patients sooner. Genetic medicines are one area where we see real potential, particularly for diseases with few or no treatment options. Chemistry, manufacturing, and controls (CMC) often sets the pace in this field. We’re hiring a CMC & Manufacturing Lead to bring deep technical expertise to our team. You’ll guide CMC strategy across a range of genetic medicine technologies, work closely with external partners, and help our researchers and engineers make Claude useful for real CMC work. Much of today’s CMC practice was built for products made at scale for large populations. You’ll help work out what better approaches could look like for smaller ones, including platform processes, faster testing, and ways to carry knowledge from one product to the next. If you have deep experience manufacturing genetic medicines and want to explore how AI can help accelerate the way they’re developed, we’d love to hear from you. Key responsibilities Guide CMC and manufacturing strategy for genetic medicines, from early development through clinical supply Serve as a CMC expert to external partners, reviewing process, analytical, and supply plans and resolving technical issues together Provide technical oversight of externally conducted process development, formulation, analytical development, fill-finish, stability, and release testing, with phase-appropriate specifications and control strategies Collaborate with scientists across disciplines to turn early research into robust, GMP-ready processes Oversee quality for externally manufactured material, including audits, quality agreements, and batch disposition Evaluate novel manufacturing, analytical, and delivery technologies, and make clear recommendations Develop approaches that reduce the time and cost of reaching clinical material without compromising product quality or patient safety Work with Anthropic researchers and engineers to identify where Claude can speed up CMC work, contribute to evaluations and tools, and test results against real-world problems Identify CMC and supply chain risks early, and communicate status, tradeoffs, and decisions clearly Minimum qualifications Biotechnology or pharmaceutical industry experience leading CMC for gene therapy, gene editing, or nucleic acid products, including taking a product from preclinical development into the clinic Deep expertise in several of the following, and working knowledge of the others: lipid nanoparticles (LNP), mRNA, guide RNA (gRNA), adeno-associated virus (AAV), and antisense oligonucleotides (ASO), including how they are manufactured, characterized, and released Deep understanding of GMP manufacturing and regulatory CMC requirements for genetic medicines, including writing or reviewing CMC sections of INDs or equivalent filings A strong track record of selecting and managing CDMOs, CROs, and other external partners, including technology transfer and quality oversight Demonstrated creativity in manufacturing novel products, shown by process, analytical, or supply solutions you developed where no established precedent existed Ability to evaluate novel technologies rigorously from data and turn that evaluation into a clear recommendation Clear written and verbal communication, including explaining CMC tradeoffs to people outside the field Curiosity about how AI can change drug development, and excitement about Anthropic’s mission to build safe and beneficial AI Preferred qualifications 10+ years in the biotechnology or pharmaceutical industry, with a focus on CMC and gene therapy product development An advanced degree in chemical engineering, biochemistry, pharmaceutical sciences, molecular biology, or a related field Experience with rare disease or small-population programs, or with platform-based manufacturing and regulatory approaches Direct experience leading CMC discussions with the FDA and other health authorities, such as the EMA and MHRA Hands-on experience with GMP quality activities, such as vendor audits, quality agreements, deviation review, and batch disposition Experience building a CMC function or working in a fully outsourced model Experience with small-batch or rapid-turnaround GMP manufacturing and accelerated release testing Experience with technical due diligence on external technologies or manufacturing partners Hands-on experience using LLM tools like Claude in your day-to-day work The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $300,000 — $320,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. The Corporate Finance team’s mission is to generate accurate and actionable insights for leadership regarding business performance, and communicate them in a way that empowers strategic decision making. We own the company’s consolidated financial picture, including forecasting, planning, and reporting. We translate operating activity into the financial narrative that leadership, the Board, and investors rely on. You will own features across the stack—from polished frontend experiences to the APIs, services, and data models that power them. This role is well suited to engineers who combine strong product judgment with broad technical depth. You should care about how quickly users can understand their financial lives, how reliably data moves through the system, and how AI can answer financial questions in a grounded, transparent, and useful way. You will work closely with product, design, research, infrastructure, security, and data integration teams to take ideas from early prototypes to reliable production experiences. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you're ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” Learn more about working at Coinbase . As a Program Lead, GFCO Performance & Enablement on the CX Compliance Operations team, you’ll build the learning and performance programs that keep our financial crime investigations accurate, consistent, and audit ready. The team delivers Transaction Monitoring, Enhanced Due Diligence, Screening, and Complaints Investigations, so readiness for complex regulated cases matters from day one. You’ll own programs from needs analysis through evaluation, and your work will show up in investigation quality, case handling efficiency, and regulatory readiness. What you’ll do: Own end-to-end delivery of onboarding, cross-skilling, and performance-improvement programs, from scoping and planning through deployment and post-launch follow-through in your workstream. Diagnose capability gaps using operational data, quality results, and stakeholder input, distinguishing skill gaps from process, tooling, or policy issues and recommending the intervention most likely to close them. Design practical learning experiences, including facilitated sessions, self-paced content, job aids, scenario-based practice, and assessments grounded in approved compliance procedures. Build and maintain program documentation, rollout materials, evaluation records, and reusable templates that strengthen delivery quality, repeatability, and auditability. Partner with subject-matter experts, operations leads, Workforce, Quality Assurance, and Data Analytics to validate content, align timelines, and report evidence-based updates on program health and results. Drive continuous improvement by capturing lessons learned, refining interventions against outcome data, and recommending when to retire programs that do not improve performance. Required Skills and Experience: 4+ years designing, delivering, or improving learning, readiness, or performance-enablement solutions in a complex regulated or operational environment such as financial crime compliance or financial services. Proven record independently leading projects end to end, including scoping, milestone planning, risk management, stakeholder coordination, and delivery follow-through. Demonstrated ability to interpret learning, quality, and operational data and translate findings into targeted interventions that improve measurable performance outcomes. Experience building practical learning content such as facilitated sessions, self-paced modules, assessments, and job aids with learning platforms and authoring tools, including validating AI-generated content against authoritative sources. Consistent success partnering cross-functionally without formal authority, including challenging unclear requirements and communicating trade-offs plainly. Preferred: experience supporting financial crime compliance operations in transaction monitoring, enhanced due diligence, screening, or complaints investigations, plus certification in instructional design, project management, or compliance. Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality. items.title: Enterprise B2B Communications Manager
items.location_text: New York, San Francisco, Washington, DC, Toronto
items.description: WHO ARE WE? Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! Role Overview Cohere is built on a simple advantage: AI that actually deploys at production-scale. With enterprise-ready products, a CEO who co-authored the Transformer Paper that launched modern AI, and the newly combined strength of Aleph Alpha, we’re becoming the transatlantic leader in sovereign AI for enterprises and governments. A company with this much momentum needs a storytelling engine to match, and this role is part of the team building it. Reporting to the Director of Corporate Communication, the Enterprise B2B Communications Manager will earn the attention and trust of business audiences by showing, through real customer stories, how organizations use Cohere to change the way they work, serve their customers, and create value. You’ll translate Cohere’s global priorities into stories that resonate with what customers and partners care about, pairing sharp strategy with consistently strong execution. You’ll partner closely with GTM, marketing, product, legal, government affairs, and sales to make it happen. Key Responsibilities As the Enterprise B2B Communications Manager, you will: - Execute an enterprise B2B communications strategy that translates company-wide priorities into a program with clear audiences, narratives and outcomes for global customers and partners. - Establish relationships with communications teams at partner and customer companies - Lead campaigns across earned and owned channels that deepen understanding of Cohere’s technology, build trust, and demonstrate business value - Create a robust library of customer, partner and ecosystem stories and testimonials that show real impact across markets and priority industries. - Shape narratives and messaging that turn complex technology and product developments into clear, compelling stories for business audiences - Lead communications for launches, executive moments and tentpole events, ensuring strong coordination across teams. - Cultivate trusted relationships with leading business, technology, trade, and new media - Advise and prepare senior spokespeople for media, speaking and stakeholder opportunities, including briefing materials and talking points - Partner closely with regional and global teams to set clear ways of working, share insight and make sure local perspectives shape overall strategy. - Spot emerging opportunities and reputational risks early, offering sound counsel and helping the team respond quickly and confidently. - Manage agency partners, holding a high bar for strategic thinking, creativity and execution. - Support an ambitious, collaborative and low-ego culture where people are comfortable being flexible and scrappy. Qualifications - 8+ years of experience in communications, ideally in AI, enterprise software, or developer‑focused environments - Are experienced in collaborating with external customers, strategic partners, and senior executives. - Have a track record of securing impactful coverage across business, technology, trade, and industry media. - Are highly organized and detail‑oriented with strong project management skills and a bias for action - Are comfortable navigating ambiguity and thrive in fast‑moving, high‑growth environments - Build strong cross‑functional relationships to drive clarity, consistency, and alignment across teams FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS: - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch. - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health. - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme. - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent. - Annual enrichment benefits: Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit. Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching. - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!) - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite. HOW AND WHERE WE WORK: - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon. - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events. - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city. - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly. If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12a6IrLdF3kI2nonKSr4tiFuz18rLQbaeYV-JM9L4o9Q/edit, and we will work together to meet your needs. We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider. Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers https://cohere.com/careers page.

items.description: ABOUT ELEVENLABS ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology. We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always. We have expanded from voice into three main platforms: - ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale. - ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages. - ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models. Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you. HOW WE WORK - High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy. - Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you. - AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations. - Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models. - Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location. WHAT WE OFFER - Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible. - Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities. - Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend. - Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose. - Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún - Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend. ABOUT THE ROLE ElevenAgents is our platform for building and running conversational AI agents at scale. items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. You won't be handed a spec. You'll come up with the bet, shape a vague idea into the leanest real version one, and ship it. Most zero-to-one bets don't work the first time, so you'll keep pushing new products over the line. If you'd rather have a clear spec and a stable surface, that's a valid preference. It's just not this team. Claude is already one of the most-used AI products in the world. What we build shapes how millions of people use AI every day. The pace is fast and the products are new. If you love building consumer products from scratch and care about getting the details right, we'd like to hear from you. Key responsibilities Originate new consumer AI product bets and own them from first idea to launch Spot the gap between what Claude can do and what people actually experience, and bring the bet: what to build, why now, and the cheapest way to test it Take a vague direction and cut it down to the leanest real version one Set technical direction for the products you build Own the quality bar for how the product looks and feels, treating latency, responsiveness, and reliability as first-class concerns Partner with privacy, security, legal, design, platform teams and external partners to find a path to launch Iterate quickly based on user feedback and internal testing Keep pushing new products over the line, since most zero-to-one bets don't work the first time Minimum qualifications Experience building consumer-facing products, with a strong emphasis on product quality and user experience Experience taking a consumer product from nothing to real users Proficiency in React, items.title: Defense Success Manager, France
items.description: ABOUT MISTRAL Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. THE ROLE As a Defense Success Manager, you own what happens to our most strategic defense and sovereign accounts after the build: you make deployed AI stick in real workflows — often in restricted or disconnected environments — keep production commitments healthy, defend renewals, and source the expansion signals that Sales closes. Mistral's Solutions teams (Deployment Strategists and Forward Deployed Engineers) co-create high-value AI use cases with customers in these environments. Your job is to make those investments successful beyond delivery — adopting what has been built, operating it with confidence, demonstrating its impact, and scaling value across the institution. You will work with mission owners, program stakeholders, end users, security and IT teams, and across Mistral with Solutions, Product, Engineering and Support. This is not a high-volume, ticket-queue customer success role. Portfolios are small and deep — typically one or two flagship accounts plus a small number of adjacent programs. It calls for a strategic account mindset, the technical judgment to navigate complex and constrained deployment environments, and the energy to build the customer success function as Mistral grows. Travel to customer sites, including secure facilities, is a regular part of the job. You will join on one of two tracks (and can move between them): - Adoption track — embedded in flagship programs while Solutions is still delivering. You own the adoption and change-management motion around the build: user waves, enablement, champions, training programs, and the evidence that proves value is landing. - Operational track — you take accounts through a structured handover once Solutions completes delivery, and own the run phase end-to-end: operational health, value realization, renewals, and expansion signals. In both tracks you operate in close partnership with Solutions: they deliver and hand over; you own post-handover; they re-engage on expansion signals. Occasionally, account teams will also pull you into late-stage pre-sales — authoring the customer training and scale-up plan that gives a buyer confidence in the rollout. WHAT YOU WILL DO OWN THE CUSTOMER SUCCESS AND VALUE PLAN - Build a clear view of each account's objectives, stakeholders, deployed use cases, commitments and risks. Translate it into a shared success plan with owners, milestones and measurable outcomes. - Establish a practical operating cadence with customer sponsors, business owners, IT and delivery teams. Lead success reviews that make progress, risks, decisions and next steps clear. - Define a baseline and track the outcomes that matter for each use case: adoption and usage against entitled seats, customer satisfaction, operational health and business impact. Turn the evidence into a clear value narrative. MAKE DEPLOYMENT REALITIES PART OF THE SUCCESS PLAN - Understand how each customer's deployment model — on-premises, VPC or serverless — affects the products and use cases they can access, operate and scale. Validate the specifics with the technical teams rather than assuming feature parity or identical operating models. - Identify the practical implications of deployment choices: security and data requirements, access and integrations, release and upgrade cadence, available features, capacity, observability and support processes. Explain the trade-offs clearly to customer and Mistral stakeholders. - Translate those constraints into an actionable adoption plan: align enablement and release communications with the version the customer actually runs, account for security approvals and upgrade windows, and agree how to measure usage when telemetry is limited. - Spot risks early, qualify their impact on adoption, renewal or value, and coordinate the right Solutions, Product, Engineering or Support owners to resolve them. Set clear expectations without making unvalidated technical or roadmap commitments. DRIVE ADOPTION, AUTONOMY AND SUSTAINED VALUE - Help customer teams move from a delivered use case to regular, effective use. Identify the users, workflows and change-management needs that determine whether it sticks. - Coordinate onboarding, training, product updates and hands-on enablement with the right Mistral and customer teams. Develop customer champions and train-the-trainer motions so adoption scales beyond direct Mistral involvement. - Prepare the transition from delivery to run: clarify operational ownership, support and escalation paths, and the resources users need to succeed independently. - Monitor adoption and customer health, investigate where usage or value is falling short, and lead a coordinated plan to address the causes. DEFEND AND GROW THE COMMERCIAL RELATIONSHIP - Own the renewal motion for your accounts: know every renewal date, the auto vs non-auto renewal terms, and the risk story behind each one. Run the renewal play early — no surprises at renewal time. - Track and improve account NRR. Identify new use cases, teams and expansion opportunities, and share them with the account team grounded in demonstrated value. - Lead business reviews with the account team: value delivered, risks owned, decisions needed, roadmap asks. BRING THE CUSTOMER VOICE INTO MISTRAL - Gather and qualify feedback from users, technical teams and sponsors. Distinguish enablement needs from product gaps, deployment constraints and support issues, and route each to the right owner. - Track important requests and communicate progress and limitations back to the customer, while Product and Engineering retain ownership of product and technical decisions. BUILD THE COMPANY AS WELL AS THE ACCOUNT - Create the playbooks, success plans, handover practices and measurement approaches that are missing. Test them with customers, improve them, and make them reusable across accounts. - Bring structure to ambiguity: identify what needs to happen, make a plan, mobilize the right people and follow through — without waiting for a perfect process or detailed instructions. - Roughly a fifth of your time is protected, rotating build time for exactly this work; it is part of the job, not extra to it. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - 5+ years of experience owning outcomes for enterprise or institutional customers of technical products or deployed solutions — adoption and commercial outcomes (retention, renewal, expansion), not relationship management or activity reporting. - Strong technical fluency in secure enterprise deployment models. You can identify what a deployment type (on-premise, disconnected, air-gapped) means for available features, telemetry, upgrades and accreditation, and you validate specifics with technical teams instead of assuming parity. - Ability to engage credibly with architects, engineers, IT and security stakeholders, while translating technical trade-offs into clear implications for mission owners and executives. You know when to bring in a deeper technical expert. - Comfort operating under security, compliance and confidentiality constraints, including restricted or classified environments and strict information-handling rules. - Strong ownership and builder energy. You have created structure or improved a process in an ambiguous, fast-moving environment and are motivated to build a company, not wait for clear directions. - Excellent communication, stakeholder management and execution skills. You align teams without formal authority, surface risks early and drive decisions through to completion - Analytical and commercially minded: you can define meaningful success metrics with imperfect data, assess customer health, and are comfortable carrying renewal and NRR accountability. NICE TO HAVE - Experience serving defense, public sector or critical infrastructure customers, including sovereign or classified programs. - Experience with AI, machine learning, data platforms or complex enterprise software, including production deployments in regulated or security-sensitive environments. - Experience working alongside deployment, engineering or professional services teams on custom use cases, and the transition from implementation to ongoing operation. - Familiarity with public procurement, framework agreements and multi-year option structures. SECURITY & COMPLIANCE CRITERIA - Eligibility: must hold citizenship in the target territory (France for now). - Clearable: must meet all local requirements for high-level security clearance (e.g. no criminal record, fulfillment of national service obligations). WHAT WE OFFER We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks. For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page https://app.notion.com/p/mistralai/Benefits-at-Mistral-36e6ba59a7fe836b93dd01737fcc27ef?source=copy_link. PRIVACY POLICY Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy https://legal.mistral.ai/terms/applicant-privacy-policy.

items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role As Anthropic grows, more of the work our own teams do every day runs through internal software, and that software has to keep up. We are building that software, and we are building it Claude-first: Claude should take on as much of the repetitive, multi-step work as it safely can, and people decide what needs a human. We’re looking for Staff+ full-stack engineers to drive this work. You’ll build across the stack: the products people use and the agents that work alongside them. You’ll work directly with the teams who rely on what you build. Many of these workflows write to business-critical data, so correctness matters as much as speed. This is a greenfield opportunity: you’ll shape the underlying systems, ship agents that take real work off people’s plates, and design how people and agents get the right context to make good decisions. Key responsibilities Design and ship internal products end to end, from the data model to the UI, for workflows that teams across Anthropic depend on. Put Claude to work on real tasks, such as gathering the context a decision needs, drafting the next step of a multi-step process or keeping records consistent across the systems teams already use, and decide where an agent should act and where a well-designed UI is the better answer. Make agents safe to trust with real work: scoped access to data, guardrails, evals, audit trails, and clear points where a person confirms before anything happens. Build one set of shared capabilities that people and agents both use, exposed as APIs and MCP tools, so the same rules and approvals apply to whoever makes the call. Treat speed and polish as product requirements. Spend time with the people who use what you build, find where their work slows down, and remove those steps. Build for correctness. When a workflow writes to business-critical data, a mistake travels into other systems, so you’ll know where idempotency, reconciliation and audit trails matter and where they don’t. Integrate with the third-party systems teams already rely on, and build the layer on top of them where people and agents get their work done. European Compute Units let enterprises commit to multi-year capacity on that infrastructure, and we are scaling toward a gigawatt of compute across Europe by 2030. You will decide how the control plane scales, how GPUs get scheduled, and how quickly a rack of bare metal becomes an on-demand cluster a customer can use. The decisions you make here shape how our infrastructure scales from today's footprint to a gigawatt, and how we turn frontier AI research into production systems used by millions. Shipped. - You have run Kubernetes in anger — and ideally built parts of it: operators, schedulers, controllers. You understand what happens underneath it, and you have worked on Linux directly, not just on managed services that sit on top of it. - You have run GPU workloads on Kubernetes, or you are confident you can own that domain fast. - You think like a developer who happens to build infrastructure, not an operator who manages it. We care less about your exact domain and more about whether you are the kind of technical force other engineers want to work alongside. items.title: Enterprise Success Manager, NL (EMEA)
items.description: ABOUT MISTRAL Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. THE ROLE As an Enterprise Success Manager at Mistral, you own what happens to our most strategic enterprise accounts after the build: you make deployed AI stick in real workflows, keep production ARR healthy, defend renewals, and source the expansion signals Sales closes. Mistral's Solutions teams create high-value AI use cases with our customers. Your job is to make those investments successful beyond delivery — adopting what has been built, operating it with confidence, measuring its business impact, and scaling value across the organization. You will work with customer sponsors, business teams, IT and security stakeholders, and across Mistral with Solutions, Product, Engineering and Support. This is not a high-volume, ticket-queue customer success role. Portfolios are small and deep. It calls for a strategic account mindset, the technical judgment to navigate complex deployment environments, and the energy to build the customer success function as Mistral grows. You will join on one of two tracks (and can move between them): - Adoption track — embedded in flagship transformations while Solutions is still delivering. You own the adoption and change-management motion around the build: user waves, enablement, champions, training programs, and the measurement that proves value is landing. - Operational track — you take accounts through a structured handover once Solutions completes delivery, and own the run phase end-to-end: operational health, value realization, renewals, and expansion signals. In both tracks you operate in close partnership with Solutions: they deliver and hand over; you own post-handover; they re-engage on expansion signals. Occasionally, account teams will also pull you into late-stage pre-sales — authoring the customer training and scale-up plan that gives a buyer confidence in the rollout, a motion already credited in a major European win. WHAT YOU WILL DO OWN THE CUSTOMER SUCCESS AND VALUE PLAN - Build a clear view of each account's objectives, stakeholders, deployed use cases, commitments and risks. Translate it into a shared success plan with owners, milestones and measurable outcomes. - Establish a practical operating cadence with customer sponsors, business owners, IT and delivery teams. Lead success reviews that make progress, risks, decisions and next steps clear. - Define a baseline and track the outcomes that matter for each use case: adoption and usage against entitled seats, customer satisfaction, operational health and business impact. Turn the evidence into a clear value narrative. MAKE DEPLOYMENT REALITIES PART OF THE SUCCESS PLAN - Understand how each customer's deployment model — on-premises, VPC or serverless — affects the products and use cases they can access, operate and scale. Validate the specifics with the technical teams rather than assuming feature parity or identical operating models. - Identify the practical implications of deployment choices: security and data requirements, access and integrations, release and upgrade cadence, available features, capacity, observability and support processes. Explain the trade-offs clearly to customer and Mistral stakeholders. - Translate those constraints into an actionable adoption plan: align enablement and release communications with the version the customer actually runs, account for security approvals and upgrade windows, and agree how to measure usage when telemetry is limited. - Spot risks early, qualify their impact on adoption, renewal or value, and coordinate the right Solutions, Product, Engineering or Support owners to resolve them. Set clear expectations without making unvalidated technical or roadmap commitments. DRIVE ADOPTION, AUTONOMY AND SUSTAINED VALUE - Help customer teams move from a delivered use case to regular, effective use. Identify the users, workflows and change-management needs that determine whether it sticks. - Coordinate onboarding, training, product updates and hands-on enablement with the right Mistral and customer teams. Develop customer champions and train-the-trainer motions so adoption scales beyond direct Mistral involvement. - Prepare the transition from delivery to run: clarify operational ownership, support and escalation paths, and the resources users need to succeed independently. - Monitor adoption and customer health, investigate where usage or value is falling short, and lead a coordinated plan to address the causes. DEFEND AND GROW THE COMMERCIAL RELATIONSHIP - Own the renewal motion for your accounts: know every renewal date, the auto vs non-auto renewal terms, and the risk story behind each one. Run the renewal play early — no surprises at renewal time. - Track and improve account NRR. Identify new use cases, teams and expansion opportunities, and share them with the account team grounded in demonstrated value. - Lead business reviews with the account team: value delivered, risks owned, decisions needed, roadmap asks. BRING THE CUSTOMER VOICE INTO MISTRAL - Gather and qualify feedback from users, technical teams and sponsors. Distinguish enablement needs from product gaps, deployment constraints and support issues, and route each to the right owner. - Track important requests and communicate progress and limitations back to the customer, while Product and Engineering retain ownership of product and technical decisions. BUILD THE COMPANY AS WELL AS THE ACCOUNT - Create the playbooks, success plans, handover practices and measurement approaches that are missing. Test them with customers, improve them, and make them reusable across accounts. - Bring structure to ambiguity: identify what needs to happen, make a plan, mobilize the right people and follow through — without waiting for a perfect process or detailed instructions. - Roughly a fifth of your time is protected, rotating build time for exactly this work; it is part of the job, not extra to it. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - 5+ years of experience in customer-facing roles, such as Customer Success, Delivery/Implementation, or Solutions Consulting, ideally in a technical AI or SaaS environment. - Experience owning outcomes for enterprise customers of technical products or deployed solutions — adoption and commercial outcomes (retention, renewal, expansion), not relationship management or activity reporting. - Strong technical fluency in enterprise deployment models. You can identify what a deployment type (on-premises, VPC, serverless) means for available features, telemetry, upgrades and security reviews, and you validate specifics with technical teams instead of assuming parity. - Ability to engage credibly with architects, engineers, IT and security teams, while translating technical trade-offs into clear business implications for executives and users. You know when to bring in a deeper technical expert. - Strong ownership and builder energy. You have created structure or improved a process in an ambiguous, fast-moving environment and are motivated to build a company, not wait for clear directions. - Excellent communication, stakeholder management and execution skills. You align teams without formal authority, surface risks early and drive decisions through to completion. - Analytical and commercially minded: you can define meaningful success metrics, assess customer health, and are comfortable carrying renewal and NRR accountability. - Fluent English; professional French strongly preferred (a significant share of our enterprise base is French-speaking). NICE TO HAVE - Experience with AI, machine learning, data platforms or complex enterprise software, including production deployments in regulated or security-sensitive environments. - Experience working alongside deployment, engineering or professional services teams on custom use cases, and the transition from implementation to ongoing operation. - Experience building adoption, change-management or customer education programs across large organizations. - Experience at a forward-deployed, solutions-led company. WHAT WE OFFER We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks. items.title: Partner Marketing Lead, APAC
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role We are seeking a Partner Marketing Lead, APAC, reporting to the Global Head of Partner Marketing, to own partner marketing end to end across a region where partners are central to how Claude reaches enterprises. As our founding APAC Partner Marketing leader, you'll set the plan for the region rather than execute one set elsewhere: you'll build the operating model, carry partner pipeline goals, and turn our work with hyperscale cloud providers, global and regional systems integrators, resellers, and technology partners into a regional go-to-market motion that creates pipeline and drives adoption of Claude. The central challenge is sequencing: ANZ, ASEAN, India, Japan, and Korea differ in their partner ecosystems, buyers, languages, and maturity. In some, local partners are the main route to enterprise customers, and India's systems integrators also deliver for customers worldwide. You'll decide where to invest first, where a global or partner-led program is enough for now, and where to wait. This role calls for the seniority to lead a regional organization and the willingness to start hands-on with a very small team, defining the regional team plan and then hiring and managing the team as headcount opens. The role covers the whole region, including Japan, where you'll build on an established Partner Marketing presence, so that partners and sales teams experience one connected regional approach. Key responsibilities Set the APAC partner marketing strategy, annual plan, and investment priorities, aligned with global Partner Marketing, the regional Partnerships business plan, and APAC sales leadership Decide which markets and partners to prioritize, in what order, and through which motions, and revisit those choices as the business changes Represent Partner Marketing with regional and global leadership, and make clear recommendations on tradeoffs Build the regional operating model, including planning, intake, approvals, reporting, and how global programs are adapted for local markets Define the regional team plan and make the case for where to add capacity Hire, manage, and develop the team as headcount opens, and set the standard for partner marketing in the region Build a network of regional agencies and vendors to extend the team Build joint marketing plans with priority partners, starting with hyperscale cloud providers and their co-sell and marketplace motions, alongside global and regional systems integrators, resellers, and technology partners Equip partners to market and sell Claude on their own, with localized campaigns, content, and workshops they can run with their own teams and customers Lead the regional partner calendar, including joint campaigns, executive engagements, workshops, partner events, and regional partner summits Set pipeline and adoption goals with Partnerships and sales leadership, and take ownership of the results Connect partner activity to priority accounts and open opportunities so that partner and direct sales motions reinforce each other Build the regional pipeline of partner customer stories and public proof points Own the regional partner marketing budget and market development funds, with strong financial discipline and a focus on return Maximize partner co-investment and negotiate effectively with vendors Define how success is measured, including sourced and influenced pipeline and adoption of Claude, and use results to decide where to invest and what to stop Align the regional plan to the International Partnerships business plan, working with its leadership on overall goals and day to day with subregional and country partnerships leaders and partner managers Work with APAC sales leaders on account priorities and where partners can help open or advance deals Coordinate with APAC Field Marketing so that field and partner programs run from one regional plan Work with global Partner Marketing on partners that span regions, such as cloud providers and global systems integrators, as well as Product Marketing, Customer Marketing, Communications, and Marketing Operations, and bring regional partner feedback back into their plans Minimum qualifications 14+ years of B2B enterprise technology marketing, with significant experience in partner or channel marketing Experience owning partner or channel marketing strategy for a region or multiple markets, including priorities and investment decisions Experience leading marketing programs across multiple Asia-Pacific markets, with strong awareness of how those markets differ Experience hiring and managing marketers, or clear leadership experience to build a regional team Experience building programs with cloud providers, systems integrators, resellers, or distributors, and an understanding of co-sell and partner-led pipeline Track record of contributing to significant pipeline or revenue goals, with strong analytics and attribution skills Experience managing substantial marketing budgets, including partner co-funding or market development funds Experience building programs and processes from the ground up, and willingness to do hands-on work while the team grows Ability to work effectively with sales leaders, partner executives, and senior stakeholders, and to move priorities forward with people you don't manage Ability to make thoughtful decisions with incomplete information, and comfort with ambiguity Clear written and verbal communication with executive and regional audiences Care about the societal impacts of AI and about helping organizations adopt AI responsibly Preferred qualifications Experience building and scaling a partner or channel marketing function in APAC at an enterprise software or cloud company Experience leading marketing with cloud providers, systems integrators, and resellers or distributors, including owning the pipeline that came from that work Experience managing a regional team across several APAC markets in partner or field marketing Experience as the first partner or field marketing leader in a new region Experience marketing AI/ML or other complex technical products to enterprises Experience marketing with AWS, Microsoft, or Google Cloud in APAC, including co-sell and marketplace motions Experience launching or scaling a reseller or partner program Established relationships with partners, agencies, or industry organizations in the region Fluency in one or more Asia-Pacific languages Knowledge of regional regulatory and compliance requirements for marketing Experience using Claude or other AI tools to scale marketing work Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

items.description: ABOUT MISTRAL Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. ABOUT THE ROLE We are looking for a Product Support & Enablement Lead to lead and develop our existing L1 Product Support team. You will help the team resolve more customer issues without escalating to L2, while improving the tools, training, and workflows that allow support to scale. This is a senior technical and people-management role—not simply a role overseeing today’s queue. You will lead frontline delivery for Product Support (L1) and develop the team’s ability to investigate and resolve increasingly technical requests, including paid self-serve and first-level enterprise issues. You will work closely with L2 and other teams to define clear ownership, identify work Product Support (L1) can safely take on, and build repeatable escalation paths. You will also contribute to operational continuity for the wider Support organization. You will be equally comfortable coaching a team member through a customer issue, investigating an API error, improving a support workflow, and partnering with Engineering or Product to address a recurring problem. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES LEAD FRONTLINE SUPPORT DELIVERY - Lead, coach, and develop a distributed L1 Product Support team, providing regular feedback and supporting technical growth. - Own day-to-day L1 Product Support delivery, including queue prioritization, backlog management, customer communication, and regional handoffs. - Define and maintain clear ownership of L1 Product Support queues and handoffs to L2, including for paid self-serve and first-level enterprise requests. - Monitor service quality, response and resolution times, backlog health, and customer satisfaction; turn insights into practical improvements. - Stay hands-on with complex or sensitive customer issues and model strong technical judgment. INCREASE PRODUCT SUPPORT (L1) TECHNICAL AUTONOMY - Train and coach Product Support (L1) agents to investigate, reproduce, and resolve more technical issues across Mistral products, including Vibe, Studio, and APIs. - Work with L2 to identify issue types that Product Support (L1) can safely take on and define the knowledge, access, and safeguards needed. - Create playbooks, troubleshooting guides, and escalation criteria that help Product Support (L1) agents resolve issues independently and consistently. - Improve L1-to-L2 handoffs so escalations contain customer impact, investigation steps, and relevant evidence. - Track escalation patterns and use them to prioritize training, documentation, and product improvements. SCALE SYSTEMS, WORKFLOWS, AND AUTOMATION - Own improvements to frontline support tooling, routing, workflows, macros, and internal processes. - Own improvements to frontline Product Support (L1) tooling, routing, workflows, macros, and internal processes. - Develop AI-assisted support and automation, including Intercom Fin, to reduce repetitive work while maintaining response quality and appropriate human escalation. - Identify recurring contact drivers and partner with Product, Engineering, and other teams to address them at the source. - Build reporting and operating reviews that make workload, service performance, escalation patterns, and risks visible. - Establish shared processes with specialist Support teams while respecting their ownership of technical delivery. BUILD KNOWLEDGE AND OPERATIONAL CONTINUITY - Develop onboarding materials and technical training that help agents become autonomous. - Work with Documentation and Product teams to keep internal guidance and customer-facing help content accurate and useful. - Share customer insights and support trends with Product, Engineering, and go-to-market teams. - Help coordinate support readiness for new products, features, and processes. - Contribute to operational continuity for the Support organization through team coordination, reporting, and escalation management. WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR - Significant experience in customer-facing technical support, product support, or support operations in a fast-moving technology environment. - Senior people-management experience, including leading, coaching, and developing a Support team. - Strong technical judgment and troubleshooting skills, including the ability to investigate product issues, reproduce bugs, and understand API requests and errors. - Experience managing support queues, escalations, service quality, and operational performance. - Experience improving workflows, tooling, or knowledge management. - Ability to use support data to identify bottlenecks and prioritize improvements without losing sight of the customer experience. - Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, including the ability to explain technical issues clearly to different audiences. - A pragmatic, collaborative approach and comfort working across time zones and functions. NICE TO HAVE - Experience with Intercom, Fin, or comparable support and AI automation tools. - Experience supporting developer tools, APIs, SaaS products, or AI applications. - Familiarity with scripting or lightweight automation. - Experience building onboarding programs, technical training, or support playbooks. - French language skills. items.title: Member of Technical Staff (Software Engineer, Cybersecurity Products)
items.location_text: San Francisco, Remote (United States), London, Belgrade, New York City
items.description: ABOUT THE ROLE Perplexity is building cybersecurity products where agents do the security work, not just assist with it. Our security team already runs agents on our own environment every day, across finding vulnerabilities, testing our defenses, securing our cloud, and responding to threats. Now we're turning that work into products for customers, and we expect those products to span application security, offensive testing, cloud security, detection and response, and areas we haven't picked yet. We're looking for a hands-on Software Engineer to build these products end to end, from the security logic and agent workflows to the integrations and product surfaces customers use. You'll ship to design partners and enterprise customers quickly, and you'll work directly with the security engineers who do this work internally, so what we build is grounded in real codebases, real environments, and real attackers. RESPONSIBILITIES - Build security products from zero to one across domains such as application security, penetration testing and offensive security, cloud security, and detection and response. - Build agents that do real security work: review code and find vulnerabilities, test applications and infrastructure like an attacker, assess cloud configurations, and investigate threats, then validate findings and recommend or apply fixes. - Build the systems underneath: multi-tenant services, data pipelines, and secure execution environments that run against customer code, cloud accounts, and telemetry. - Build integrations with the tools customers already use: source control and CI/CD, cloud providers, identity providers, security tools, ticketing, and chat. - Ship the product surfaces customers use: APIs, dashboards, onboarding, and workflows that fit how security and engineering teams actually work. - Hold the product to the same standard we hold ourselves: strong tenant isolation, least privilege, safe handling of customer secrets and data, and tight controls on any agent that acts in a customer environment. - Define how we measure quality (finding accuracy, false positive rate, exploitability, time to fix, cost) and use it to drive improvements. - Work directly with design partners and customers, and help decide which security problems we should build products for next. QUALIFICATIONS - 4+ years of experience as a software engineer building production systems, with meaningful time spent on security products, security data platforms, or security engineering with heavy software development. - Proficiency in at least one major programming language (such as Python, Go, TypeScript, or Rust) and experience owning production services end to end. - Hands-on depth in at least one security domain, such as application security, penetration testing or offensive security, cloud security, or detection and response, and curiosity to work across the others. - Experience integrating with security- or developer-relevant systems such as source control, CI/CD, cloud provider APIs, identity providers, scanners, or SIEMs. - Familiarity with cloud infrastructure (AWS preferred) and building secure, multi-tenant SaaS. - Comfortable working directly with customers and shipping pragmatic improvements quickly in an ambiguous, early-stage product area. - Bonus: experience building LLM-powered agents, evaluation frameworks, or tool-using automation for security or other high-stakes domains. - Bonus: experience at a security product company (AppSec, pentesting, cloud security, detection and response) or on an internal security platform at scale.
